provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
In the original task a 10x21 grid has a full-height divider column of colour 5. It sits between two 10x10 panels. The right panel copies the left one except that 1-2 dots have moved. The output is the left (source) panel, recoloured in two ways. A cell that is filled in the source but background in the other panel becomes 2 (vacated). A cell that is background in the source but filled in the other panel becomes 1 (arrived).

Under the D4 transform (row reversal first for indices >= 4, then d4%4 clockwise rotations), the divider becomes a full column for even d4 and a full row for odd d4. The source panel lands at: 0 left, 1 top, 2 right, 3 bottom, 4 right, 5 bottom, 6 left, 7 top. Both panels undergo the same rigid motion, so in visible coordinates the panels stay start-aligned. Visible panel cell j on one side corresponds to cell j on the other side, a translation by divider+1.

The emitted program uses a different code path for each axis rather than transposing. It locates the divider as the full line of palette[5], choosing the one nearest the centre and falling back to the midline. It takes the source panel on the specialised side and compares it pixelwise with the other panel, using palette[0] as background. It then writes palette[2] at vacated cells and palette[1] at arrived cells. Unmoved dots and background keep the source panel's values.
draft_notes.limitations:
No tests have been run by me; the factory and emitted programs have not been executed against the fixtures or fresh pairs.

The constructor's domain is fixed: 10x21 grids, divider at index 10, equal 10-wide panels. If panels were unequal, the emitted program compares only the overlapping start-aligned region and leaves the rest of the source panel unchanged; this situation never occurs in the generator.

Background is taken as palette[0] rather than inferred.

The generator excludes colours 1, 2 and 5 from dots, and its draw() overlap checks guarantee that vacated and arrived cells never coincide with other dots in either panel. Because of this, the pixelwise panel difference exactly reproduces the generator's labels, with no tie or ordering ambiguity.

I found no fixture contradictions or constructor defects.

independent_source_review.mechanism: The input is a 10x21 grid with a full-height divider of colour 5 at column 10 and two equal 10x10 panels. The right panel copies the left panel's dots except for 1-2 dots, each shifted by a nonzero offset with |dr|,|dc|<=2 that is not (±2,±2). The output is the left (source) panel with three kinds of cell: source-nonbackground and other-background cells become 2 (vacated); source-background and other-nonbackground cells become 1 (arrived); all other cells keep the source value. The emitted solver locates the full palette[5] line in visible coordinates (column for even d4, row for odd d4). It picks the source panel by a specialised side flag and applies the pixelwise panel difference with palette[0], palette[2] and palette[1].
evidence: Label correctness. draw() writes output[row][col] for unmoved dots, and writes 2 at the origin and 1 at the destination for moved dots. Several checks make these positions distinct: common.overlaps with 2x2 boxes keeps all source dots at Chebyshev distance >= 2 from each other; output[row+rdiff][col+cdiff] != 0 and output[row][col] != 0 make unmoved positions, moved origins and moved destinations pairwise distinct in output space, whatever the processing order. Consequently L!=bg & R==bg holds exactly at moved origins, and L==bg & R!=bg holds exactly at moved destinations. The pixelwise difference therefore reproduces the constructor labels exactly, with no hidden latent and no ties.

Colours. Dot colours come from random_colors(..., exclude=[1,2,5]), so dots never collide with the vacated/arrived colours or the divider colour. A moved dot cannot land on its own origin because the (0,0) offset is rejected. 'Only one of each color moves' is a generator-side constraint only; the label rule does not depend on it.

Bounds. Destinations are checked to lie in 0..9 before the right panel is written at col+cdiff+11 (columns 11..20), so the divider at column 10 is never overwritten. No dot column or row can be a full line of palette[5], since that colour is excluded, so the divider is unique.

Orientation mapping. The factory's side table is 0 L, 1 T, 2 R, 3 B, 4 R, 5 B, 6 L, 7 T. This is internally consistent with D4 = horizontal flip (for d4>=4) followed by d4%4 clockwise rotations: d4=4 flips L to R; d4=5 rotates R to B; d4=7 rotates R to T. The host audit (8000 augmented pair checks, 16 fixture variants) confirms it against the actual augmentation.

Panel alignment. The panels are equal width and both undergo the same rigid map, so visible local index j in one panel corresponds to local index j in the other. The [:n] start-aligned comparison is therefore correct in every orientation.

Direct solving. The solver works directly in augmented visible coordinates with separate column and row code paths. There is no untransform/native-solve/retransform wrapper. The specialised constants are genuine rule colours (background, divider, vacated 2, arrived 1) and a demonstrated side orientation.

Episode evidence. There is no arbitrary colour lookup. The vacated and arrived colours appear in every demonstration, because each demo moves at least one dot. Source side and divider orientation are spatial constants that are visible in the demonstrations, since output size and content equal one panel.

Fixtures. The three train fixtures and the test fixture are reproduced by validate() parameters and are consistent with the archived rule: pair1 (3,5)->2, (3,4)->1, (8,7)->2, (7,6)->1; test (0,4)->2, (1,6)->1, (4,6)->2, (5,5)->1.
nonblocking_limits: Background is fixed as palette[0] rather than inferred. This matches the constructor domain, which uses an all-zero background.
The midline fallback (no divider found) and the unequal-panel handling ([:n] overlap) are defensive paths that the constructor never reaches.
The divider check grid[row+rdiff][col+cdiff] inspects the left panel, not the right. This is harmless because the output-space checks already guarantee that all relevant positions are distinct.

The D4 side table is verified only against the host's augmentation convention, read as horizontal flip then clockwise rotation. It was not derived independently from a documented transform spec; the host audit pass is the confirming evidence.
required_context_checks: Confirm the host's D4 convention for indices >= 4 is a horizontal (left-right) flip followed by d4%4 clockwise quarter-turns, matching the factory's source-side table. The supplied 8000 augmented checks suggest it is.

Confirm the palette permutation is applied consistently to the demos and the query, so that palette[1], palette[2] and palette[5] remain the arrived, vacated and divider colours in visible coordinates.
